input.purpose: Measure the served Lab air volume V_lab from the occupied-source CO2 rise and scrubber-driven concentration decay.
hypotheses: The Lab is a single well-mixed zone during the test.
The hatch remains closed throughout; exchange through the closed hatch is not measured and is assumed small enough not to bias the fitted time constant.
The one Lab occupant, FE-3, remains in the Lab at steady activity for the entire test; any entry or exit invalidates the curve.
A first volume guess of 30 m3 and full-speed effective flow of 1 m3/min give an estimated decay time constant of 30 min.
The scrubber effective flow scales with commanded speed and its registered full-speed effective flow is valid.
Fit the decay to C(t)=C_eq+(C_0-C_eq)exp(-t/tau), not to zero; calculate V_lab=Qe*tau.

monitoring.reason: The occupied-zone test deliberately raises CO2; monitor FE-3 throughout, including loss of signal.

steps.why: Hold the Lab as one zone and reduce effective flow so occupant CO2 rises several hundred ppm above sensor noise; record Lab and Hab-B CO2, speed acceptance, and occupancy at one-minute intervals.
Return to full speed and record the decay at one-minute intervals for about one estimated time constant; fit toward the nonzero equilibrium and derive V_lab=Qe*tau.

abort.when: Lab CO2 is at or above 3000 ppm.
The scrubber refuses either commanded speed.
Battery state of charge is under 35 percent.
FE-3 is outside 45–120 bpm, monitoring is lost, or any additional person enters the Lab.

expected.rise: From the measured 1200 ppm start, Lab CO2 should rise by several hundred ppm during the 30 percent phase while remaining below 2800 ppm.
expected.decay: At 100 percent speed, Lab CO2 should follow a monotonic exponential approach to a nonzero equilibrium after scrubber lag.
expected.volume: Fit tau from the full-speed segment and compute V_lab=Qe*tau using the registered effective flow at full speed; the 30 m3 value is only the pre-test duration estimate.
expected.connectedZone: Hab-B CO2 should not show a correlated transient comparable to the Lab curve while the hatch is closed.
expected.falsification: A person entering or leaving, a speed refusal, failure to rise above noise, non-exponential decay after lag, or a correlated Hab-B transient falsifies the stated conditions and invalidates the volume result.

justifications.reason: Operational ceiling below signed abort ceiling.
Signed minimum battery state of charge.
